cases.answer: Appetite hormones: sleep loss/restriction is linked to higher ghrelin and lower leptin (raised ghrelin/leptin ratio; e.g. 14% higher ghrelin in short sleepers; evening ghrelin rise in 19 lean men with leptin unaffected in that trial), plus increased endocannabinoid levels (2-AG, 2-OG). Separate glucose/insulin findings: in 11 young men restricted to 4 h sleep for 6 nights, glucose clearance fell 40% and insulin response was 30% lower versus recovery sleep, a prediabetic state; in 38 women, a 6-week short-sleep period increased insulin resistance versus extended sleep, independent of adiposity.

cases.answer: In Lebedeva et al., ZnT7 (perinuclear region/Golgi of rat kidney tubular epithelial cells) is shown to inhibit high-glucose-induced EMT when overexpressed; its knockdown promotes EMT and is accompanied by activation of MAPK/ERK and TGF-β/Smad pathways; SLC30A7 also has antioxidant effects against glucose-induced apoptosis via NFE2L2/HMOX1. ZnT8 is highly expressed in kidney (mainly tubular epithelium, weakly in glomerulus/podocytes) and protects against EMT and tubulointerstitial fibrosis by restraining TGF-β1/Smads signalling, and against tubular apoptosis via TNFAIP3 induction and NF-κB suppression.

cases.answer: Lebedeva et al. is a narrative review of mechanistic, largely experimental/animal and cell data: zinc modulates HIF-1α (promotes its proteasomal degradation and inhibits nuclear translocation, reducing HIF-1α/VEGF signalling, angiogenesis, inflammation and fibrosis; zinc given in DKD animal models lowered fibrotic markers and HIF-1α expression). These are proposed pathways, not clinical effect estimates. The Taiwan cohort (Int J Med Sci 2024) is a real-world retrospective, observational cohort of CKD stage 3–5 patients on ACEI/ARB, where SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower ESRD/dialysis risk (aHR 0.35, 95% CI 0.19–0.67), no significant association with AKI/AKD, and higher genitourinary infection risk. It is an epidemiological association with possible allocation/prescription bias and unmeasured confounding, and does not examine zinc or HIF mechanisms. (Lebedeva also notes SGLT2 inhibitor renoprotection may relate to hypoxia signalling, but that is a separate review statement, not the cohort's finding.)

cases.answer: Because the three cohorts (CHARLS, ELSA, HRS) used different sleep-quality instruments and response formats, harmonization was done at the construct level rather than raw-score equivalence. Sleep quality was a single-item frequency of poor sleep in CHARLS, a sleep-complaint score in ELSA, and a modified four-item Jenkins Sleep Scale in HRS, with cohort-specific cut-offs for good/fair/poor. Baseline years also differed (ELSA 2008–09, HRS 2010, CHARLS 2011), possibly affecting healthcare access and diagnostics, so the authors say effect sizes should be compared across cohorts with caution. Estimates (good vs poor sleep quality, Model 3) were CHARLS HR 0.79 (0.65–0.97), ELSA HR 0.76 (0.60–0.98), HRS HR 0.84 (0.70–1.00, P=0.056, not significant); analyses were done separately within each cohort.
